title: Reciprocal roots, weights and integrality
statement:
With $P_i\in\Z[T]$, $P_i(0)=1$, the integral factor that [sk-thm-intfactors] produces
later put $b_i=\deg P_i$ and $P_i^{\#}(U)=U^{b_i}P_i(U^{-1})$. (Nothing here
depends on that theorem: wherever these notions are used before it, they are
applied to the $\ell$-adic factors $P_{i,\ell}$, whose roots in $\Qlb$ are
viewed in $\C$ through a fixed embedding $\iota:\Qlb\hookrightarrow\C$.) A
*reciprocal root* is a root $\alpha\in\overline{\Q}$ of $P_i^{\#}$, and
$\beta=\alpha^{-1}$ is the corresponding *ordinary root*. A reciprocal root
$\alpha$ is a *$q$-Weil number of weight $i$* if $|\tau(\alpha)|=q^{i/2}$ for every embedding
$\tau:\Q(\alpha)\hookrightarrow\C$.

For integers $q,w\ge0$, a polynomial $P\in\C[T]$ is *pure of weight $w$*
(for $q$) if $P(0)=1$ and every complex root $z$ of $P$ satisfies
$|z|=q^{-w/2}$, i.e. every reciprocal root has absolute value $q^{w/2}$. A
complex number $z$ is *universally pure of weight $w$* if it is algebraic
over $\Q$ and every complex root of its minimal polynomial over $\Q$ has
absolute value $q^{-w/2}$; a polynomial $P\in\C[T]$ is *universally pure of
weight $w$* if $P(0)=1$ and every complex root of $P$ is universally pure of
weight $w$.

The *Betti numbers* are $b_i=\deg P_i$, the *determinant constants* are
$D_i=(-1)^{b_i}[T^{b_i}]P_i(T)$, and the *Euler characteristic* of a family
$P_0,\dots,P_{n}$ of polynomials is the alternating degree sum
$\chi=\sum_{i=0}^{n}(-1)^{i}\deg P_i$.
Let $K$ be a field. For $C(T)=\sum_{n\ge0}c_nT^{n}\in K[[T]]$ the *Hankel matrix* is
$\mathcal H(C)=(c_{r+s})_{r,s\ge0}$ and its *Hankel rank* is the rank of
this (possibly infinite) matrix. The *shift span* of a sequence
$c=(c_n)_{n\ge0}$ in a ring $R$ is the $R$-submodule of $R^{\Z_{\ge0}}$
spanned by all its shifts $(c_{n+m})_{n\ge0}$, $m\ge0$ (the rows of
$\mathcal H(C)$). A *normalized integral presentation* is a
pair $A,B\in\Z[T]$ with $Z=A/B$, $A(0)=B(0)=1$ and $\gcd(A,B)=1$ in $\Q[T]$.

The polynomial, coefficient, and degree conventions are [def-weil-polynomial-ring] and [def-weil-polynomial-coefficient]; the displayed reversal is [def-weil-reverse-polynomial], and roots in an extension field are evaluated as in [def-weil-polynomial-root]. Fix algebraic closures as in [def-weil-algebraic-closure]; $\Ql$ means the field of [def-weil-l-adic-numbers]. The mention of [sk-thm-intfactors] is a forward pointer only: the definitions take the polynomials as given and do not construct the integral factors or require that theorem. The $\ell$-adic use means the same polynomial formulas with coefficients in $\Ql$ and roots in its chosen algebraic closure, with $P_{i,\ell}(0)=1$; the fixed $\iota$ is a field embedding, not a continuous or valuation-preserving embedding. In the Weil-number clause, $q$ is the fixed prime power and the condition is [def-weil-numbers]; absolute value is [def-weil-complex-absolute-value]. In the purity clauses the exponent is a real exponent: for $q>0$ use [def-weil-real-power], and at $q=0$ use $0^0=1$ and $0^r=0$ for $r\ne0$. Algebraicity is [def-weil-algebraic-element], and the minimal polynomial is [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], evaluated in $\mathbf C$ through the coefficient inclusion $\mathbf Q\subset\mathbf C$.

For the alternating degree sum of an arbitrary polynomial family, degree means natural degree, with degree zero for the zero polynomial; for all normalized polynomials above the polynomial is nonzero and this agrees with its usual degree. The Hankel matrix and its infinite rank use [def-weil-hankel-matrix]: the rank is the supremum in $\mathbf N\cup\{\infty\}$ of the ranks of finite square submatrices. The shift span is explicitly $\operatorname{span}_R\{(c_{n+m})_{n\ge0}:m\ge0\}$ using [def-weil-submodule-span] on the module of sequences with pointwise operations. In the normalized integral presentation, $Z\in1+T\mathbf Z[[T]]$ is a rational series, $A/B$ is interpreted by $BZ=A$ in $\mathbf Z[[T]]$, and coprimality is in $\mathbf Q[T]$, exactly as in [def-weil-normalized-integral-fraction].

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q35-672ba106d (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, the new node and all 14 cited statements in full. It adds only explicit conventions: K is a field for the Hankel rank (def-weil-hankel-matrix needs one), 0^0=1 and 0^r=0 at q=0 (as in Real.rpow; def-weil-real-power covers only x>0), and natDegree with 0 for the zero polynomial. The minimal polynomial comes from the general first sentence of def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension, with no separability imported. P(0)=1 makes every reciprocal root nonzero, as def-weil-numbers needs. sk-thm-intfactors is only a forward pointer and is not in stmt_deps. The closure of the item (91 nodes) is acyclic, with nothing missing or merged.
